The SAM file contains 12 reads exercising simple matches, insertions (I), soft clips (S), deletions (D), intron skips (N), mismatches via MD:Z: tag within M operations, mismatches via X CIGAR op, hard clips (H), reverse-strand reads (flag 0x10), and overlapping reads for depth counting.",
  "instruction_summary": "Fix /app/sam_coverage.py so it correctly computes per-base reference coverage and a substitution-mismatch report from SAM files, conforming to the SAM Format Specification v1.6 (https://samtools.github.io/hts-specs/SAMv1.pdf). The script is invoked as: python3 /app/sam_coverage.py <sam_file> <coverage_file> <mismatch_file>. Output format: (1) coverage file — tab-separated columns: reference_name, position, depth; positions are 1-based; only positions with depth > 0. (2) mismatch file — tab-separated columns: reference_name, position, reference_base, read_base, count; positions are 1-based; only substitution mismatches (read base differs from reference base); deletions/insertions are structural, NOT substitution mismatches, and must NOT appear. Coverage counts how many reads span each reference position (a position is spanned by any CIGAR operation that consumes the reference: M, D, N, =, X). The MD:Z: optional field encodes reference bases at mismatch and deletion positions for reads whose CIGAR uses M. When CIGAR uses = and X instead of M, = denotes match and X denotes mismatch at that reference position. Test data is at /app/data/alignments.sam.",
  "solution_outline": [
    "Fix the POS handling: SAM POS is 1-based; output positions must also be 1-based. Remove the pos-1 conversion that shifts output to 0-based.",
    "Fix CIGAR I (insertion): I consumes query only, NOT reference. Remove coverage increment and ref_pos advancement for I operations.",
    "Fix CIGAR S (soft clip): S consumes query only, NOT reference. Remove coverage increment and ref_pos advancement for S operations.",
    "Fix CIGAR D (deletion): D consumes reference only. Add coverage increments for D positions (they ARE spanned by the read).",
    "Fix CIGAR N (intron skip): N consumes reference only. Add coverage increments for N positions (they ARE spanned by the read).",
    "Implement MD:Z: tag parsing for mismatch detection within M CIGAR operations. M means 'alignment match' (could be match or mismatch); the MD tag identifies which M positions are mismatches and provides the reference base.",
    "Handle X CIGAR operations as explicit mismatches: record each X position with the read base and reference base (from MD tag).",
    "Ensure D and N positions appear in coverage but NOT in mismatches (no read base to compare).",
    "Ensure I and S positions do not appear in either coverage or mismatches (they don't consume reference)."
  ],

Verifies all fixes generalize beyond shipped data."

  "failure_modes": "An agent might fix the 0-based position bug but miss that I and S should not consume reference (or vice versa), passing some tests but failing others. An agent might parse the MD tag but mishandle the ^ deletion syntax within it, causing incorrect mismatch positions. An agent might forget that N (intron skip) consumes reference like D does, since N is rarer. An agent might incorrectly reverse-complement the read sequence for reverse-strand reads (SEQ is already on the reference strand in SAM). An agent might report deletion positions as mismatches (with a dummy read base), conflating structural differences with substitutions. Each of these corresponds to a specific SAM spec detail that the instruction names but does not explain.",

    {
      "detail": "SAM POS field is 1-based leftmost mapping position of the first CIGAR operation that consumes the reference",
      "standard_ref": "SAM v1.6 Section 1.4, field POS",
      "common_mistake": "Treating POS as 0-based, shifting all output positions by -1; or converting to 0-based internally but forgetting to convert back for output",
      "hidden_test_input": "A read at POS=1 with 3M should cover reference positions 1, 2, 3 — not 0, 1, 2"
    },
    {
      "detail": "CIGAR operation I (insertion) consumes the query but NOT the reference — inserted bases have no corresponding reference position",
      "standard_ref": "SAM v1.6 Section 1.4.2, Table 3: I consumes query only",
      "common_mistake": "Incrementing the reference position counter for I, creating phantom coverage at non-existent reference positions and shifting downstream positions",
      "hidden_test_input": "A read with 5M2I3M at POS=10 covers ref positions 10–14 and 15–17 (8 positions); the 2I should not add coverage at any ref position"
    },
    {
      "detail": "CIGAR operation S (soft clip) consumes the query but NOT the reference — soft-clipped bases are present in SEQ but not aligned",
      "standard_ref": "SAM v1.6 Section 1.4.2, Table 3: S consumes query only",
      "common_mistake": "Counting soft-clipped bases as covering reference positions, overcounting coverage at alignment boundaries",
      "hidden_test_input": "A read with 3S5M at POS=20 covers only ref positions 20–24; positions 17–19 must not appear"
    },
    {
      "detail": "CIGAR operation D (deletion from reference) consumes the reference — the read spans those reference positions (coverage includes them) but has no query bases there",
      "standard_ref": "SAM v1.6 Section 1.4.2, Table 3: D consumes reference only",
      "common_mistake": "Not counting D positions as covered; confusing 'no read base' with 'not spanned by the read'",
      "hidden_test_input": "A read with 3M5D3M at POS=10 covers ref positions 10–17 (8 positions); the 5 D positions 13–17 must have depth ≥ 1"
    },
    {
      "detail": "CIGAR operation N (skipped region/intron) consumes the reference — like D, these positions are spanned by the alignment and contribute to coverage",
      "standard_ref": "SAM v1.6 Section 1.4.2, Table 3: N consumes reference only",
      "common_mistake": "Confusing N with I (both involve 'skipping'), resulting in N positions not being counted as covered",
      "hidden_test_input": "A read with 2M100N2M at POS=5 covers ref positions 5–108 (104 positions); all 100 N positions must have depth 1"
    },
    {
      "detail": "CIGAR M means 'alignment match' — the base aligns to the reference but could be a match or mismatch; the MD:Z: tag identifies which M positions are mismatches and provides the reference base",
      "standard_ref": "SAM v1.6 Section 1.4.2 (M/op) and Section 1.5 (MD:Z: optional field)",
      "common_mistake": "Assuming M always means the bases match; not parsing the MD tag; the MD tag format uses numbers for runs of matches, single letters for substitution reference bases, and ^letters for deleted reference bases",
      "hidden_test_input": "A read with 6M CIGAR and MD:Z:3A2 means positions 1–3 match, position 4 has ref base A (mismatch with read), positions 5–6 match"
    },
    {
      "detail": "CIGAR X means 'sequence mismatch' — the read base explicitly differs from the reference base at that position; = means explicit match",
      "standard_ref": "SAM v1.6 Section 1.4.2, Table 3: = (match) and X (mismatch) consume both query and reference",
      "common_mistake": "Not recording X positions as mismatches; treating X like M (which needs MD tag); or ignoring =/X entirely",
      "hidden_test_input": "A read with 3=2X1= at POS=50 has mismatches at positions 53 and 54"
    },
    {
      "detail": "Deletion positions (D, N) must appear in coverage but NOT in the mismatch report — a deletion is a structural difference (no read base), not a substitution",
      "standard_ref": "SAM v1.6 Section 1.4.2: D and N consume reference but not query; a substitution mismatch requires both a reference base and a differing read base",
      "common_mistake": "Reporting deletion positions as mismatches with a sentinel read base like '-' or 'N'",
      "hidden_test_input": "A read with 2M3D2M — the 3 D positions must appear in coverage.tsv but must NOT appear in mismatches.tsv"

Coverage ground truth is computed from pysam's get_aligned_pairs(matches_only=False): every tuple where ref_pos is not None contributes to coverage at that 1-based position. Mismatch ground truth is computed from get_aligned_pairs(matches_only=True, with_seq=True): positions where the query base differs from the reference base (case-insensitive) are substitution mismatches. The script's output is compared position-by-position to these pysam-computed values. For the shipped SAM file, expected values are hardcoded based on manual analysis verified against pysam.",
